questions.question: should I treat my boots out of box ? Annnnd how often should I treat them ?

hybrid.answer:
**Short answer:** It depends on the boot. For Blundstones that are already pretreated, he says don't treat them out of the box. For distressed styles like Rustic Brown, he recommends conditioning them. For how often, his latest view (2022) is to go by how the leather looks and feels rather than a fixed schedule.

**Out of the box (2019 videos)**
- Reading Blundstone's own FAQ, he says most Blundstones come pretreated, so the brand doesn't recommend treating them at first, and fresh treatment would just roll off. [1]
- The exceptions are the distressed leathers (Rustic Brown, Crazy Horse, Rustic Black), which don't get the same pretreatment. The FAQ says you may treat these but don't have to. [2]
- His own view on those distressed boots is that you should condition them, and he says so emphatically. [3]
- In his review he adds that the boots are only water resistant out of the box because they're treated, and you have to keep them treated. [4]

**How often**
- **2022 (latest):** He admits he probably does it too little and does it when he feels they need it. [5] He says to judge by the boots: if they look or feel dry, or water isn't beading on top, they need more wax or oil, and if they're dirty, clean them. [6]
- **2019:** He was more specific. He said leather you haven't conditioned in a few months should definitely be conditioned. [7] He also said heavy use could mean waxing as often as every month, maybe every week, if you go crazy with your boots. [8]

He hasn't given a single fixed schedule. His rule is to treat when the leather looks or feels dry or stops beading water.

questions.question: So if I buy the levis 501 shrink to fit will they get tighter after washing?

hybrid.answer:
Yes, they get tighter, but mainly the first time you get them wet, and he says the waist loosens again with wear. His latest advice (2025) is to go about two sizes up, because they shrink [1].

**Shrinking (2023):** In his Wrangler comparison, his shrunk 501 STFs came out smaller than regular rinsed 501s [2]. He says not to put them in the dryer or rinse them in very hot water, and then you can get "a really nice fit" [3]. He thinks that with frequent wear they would stretch out to about the same size as the others [4]. He says nothing about whether further washes after that keep shrinking them.

**Sizing:** In 2021 he said Levi's advice to size up two in the waist and about two inches in length is correct, and that if you follow it the pants fit regularly after they get wet [5][6].

**He changed his mind on sizing:**
- In 2019 he ignored Levi's advice and bought a 29 waist [7].
- The waist shrank very tight at first, but a week later it had stretched enough to wear a belt [8].
- By 2020 he was glad he went small for the waist. They had been barely wearable at first, but now fit really well [9]. He did say he would have gotten a longer length [9].
- In 2021 he said it took him four pairs to learn that Levi's sizing advice is right [5].

questions.question: I'm usually a 33x30 in Levi's 502s, what size should I buy in these? [501 STF]

hybrid.answer:
Applying his rule to your numbers, a **35 waist x 32 length** in the 501 STF. He consistently says to go two sizes up in the waist and two inches longer. He hasn't said anything about how 502s compare with 501s, so I'm working from your 502 size as a stand-in for your normal size.

**His current advice (most recent first)**
- In 2025 he says of the shrink-to-fit 501: "You should usually go two sizes up." [1]
- In 2023 he sized a 30 up two sizes to a 32 and noted the tag waist doesn't match the true measurement, which is why you size up two. [2]
- In 2021 he says Levi's advice is right: go up two in the waist and two inches longer in length. [3]

**He changed his mind on this**
In 2019 he ignored Levi's advice and bought a 29x30 because jeans are usually too long on him. [4] By 2020 he said the 29 waist was so tight at first he could barely breathe, and that he would definitely have gotten a 32 length. [5] By 2021 he said following Levi's advice is correct. [3]

**Fit after shrinking**
He says that if you size up two in the waist and one step (two inches) in length, the pants will fit normally once wet. [3] In 2023 he added not to put STFs in very hot water or the dryer, because that was why his shrunk pair looked so much better. [6]

**Not covered:** he doesn't say whether odd waist sizes like 35 exist in the 501 STF. He raised a similar issue for a 34 going to a 36. [3] If a 35 isn't available, he hasn't said which way to round.

questions.question: Why do you cuff your jeans?

hybrid.answer:
He cuffs mainly because of length and style: too-long jeans look bad to him, and cuffing suits his style better than wider, uncuffed legs. He doesn't always cuff, though. With boots he now prefers his jeans worn down over them.

**Most recent (2020, Levi's 501 STF update):** He says he cuffed the 501s because he doesn't think his current style "lends itself to not cuffed wider legged pants." [1] He adds that he would have bought a 32 length, so the cuff also covers the fact that the jeans came up short for him. [1]

**Late 2019 (L.L. Bean boots):** He says he used to always cuff his jeans, but he now likes them over his boots more. He thinks that calms the boots down as a loud fashion statement. [2]

**Mid 2019 (first 501 STF video):** He says it's "all about length" for him, and jeans that look too long just look bad. In that video the basic cuff made the wide, unshrunk 501s fit and feel a little better. He also says the cuff can't be too thick. [3]

questions.question: So do you prefer [the Red Wing 3335s] over the 1907s?

hybrid.answer:
**Mostly yes, though he has hedged since.** In 2022 he called the 3335s his favorite boots ever, ahead of the 1907s. By September 2023 he said they "still might be" his favorite Red Wings, but the line that follows is garbled and he softened it, saying the 1907s and others have characteristics he really likes.

**Latest (Sept 2023):** He says he is on record that the 3335s are his favorite Red Wings, then hedges: "they still might be but they probably not the 875s the 1907s the iron Rangers all have their own characteristics that I really really like" [1]. He still likes the 3335s for being stitch-down, lighter and more nimble for walking or a light hike [2]. They were on his sell list anyway, to cut down the collection [2]. He hasn't said what he's doing with his 1907s in these videos.

**Oct 2022:** This is where he was clearest. The 3335s are his favorite boots he's ever had, and he says they "beat the 1907s" and the 875s [3]. His reasons:
- He isn't doing heritage work, just hiking and walking in the woods, so he calls them a dramatically better all-around boot [3].
- He prefers their Vibram mini lug sole to the crepe soles on the 875s and 1907s, which he doesn't think will break down as fast [4].

The caveat is toughness. The 1907s and 875s are more beefily constructed, so if you need a tough boot he says the 3335s probably aren't the ones to go for [5].

**Sept 2021 (earlier):** He had called the 1907s Red Wing's best heritage boots "by far" and said to get them if you're looking at a moc toe Red Wing [6]. That was a verdict about moc toes specifically, before he praised the 3335s.

questions.question: How do you feel bout blunnies as of Late 2023?

hybrid.answer:
As of September 2023, he's still a big fan of Blundstones, but he's retiring his well-worn 585s and letting go of the heavy-duty Extremes, mainly to make room in a shrinking boot collection.

**His 2023 view (Sept 2023)**
- He says of the 585s, the boots from his very first video, that they've "held up through it all" and stayed "probably my most water resistant boots," and that Blundstones "are just incredible. I'm a big fan of them. I've always loved them." [1] He notes some people really don't like them. [1]
- Even so, he says "it's time to retire those bunnies." [1] The reason is culling the collection, not disappointment with the boots. [2]
- The heavy-duty Blundstone work boots (the 989 Extreme series) are going too. He says they add about two inches to his height, and he'd thought they were waterproof but they're just very water-resistant nubuck. [3]
- He groups Blundstones with other slip-ons as shoes he can "flop on really quick" whatever the weather, whether he's running errands or it's raining. He's keeping a slip-on pair, though he admits it "could easily" go on the sell list. [4]

**Where he started (May 2019)**
- In his first-impressions review he recommended them "100%" if you'll keep them treated. If you won't, he says to get plastic or Gore-Tex boots instead. [5]
- He called them his favorite of the three or four boots he had at the time. [6]

Overall, his opinion of Blundstones stayed positive from 2019 to 2023. What changed is that he's now thinning out his collection.

questions.question: I'm wondering if you still have these boots and how are they holding up??? [Blundstones]

hybrid.answer:
**Mostly no.** In his most recent video on the subject (September 2023), he says it's time to retire his well-worn Blundstone 585s as part of cutting down his boot collection [1]. He also says his heavy-duty Blundstone work boots "have to go" [2].

**One possible exception.** He says he keeps a quick slip-on pair for errands and rain, and that Blundstones and similar slip-ons fall in that category. He adds that he could easily put them on the sell list [3]. The transcript doesn't make clear which pair he means.

**How the 585s held up (2023).** He says the leather is all beat up and very shiny, with old wax and conditioner on it, but that they "held up through it all" [4]. He also calls them probably his most water-resistant boots through it all [5].

**Earlier checkpoints:**
- **After 2 years (2022).** He had worn them from when it gets cold until mid-spring [6]. He restored them with cleaning, salve, oil and wax to treat cracked, dry leather [7].
- **After 1 year (2020).** He said they looked great, with more scuffs than expected, and elastics a little looser but still tight [8]. He also said he would pick a smoother leather over the rustic nubuck if he did it again [9].

**Overall.** He's still a fan, saying Blundstones are "just incredible" [5]. But in 2022 he said his Red Wing 3335s beat his Blundstones as his favorite boots [10].

questions.question: How does the made in England boot stack up to Solovairs? [Dr. Martens]

hybrid.answer:
He leans toward Solovair for value. He thinks the Made in England Dr. Martens are mainly worth it for big Dr. Martens fans, and he still liked his Solovairs in 2023 despite some problems.

**Most recent view (2023)**
- In Sept 2023 he says of his Solovair monkey boots that "through all of that I really like these boots." He had a quality-control problem with them. The fit feels loose, which he thinks probably means he sized wrong. He would sell them only to buy another pair of monkey boots [1].
- In May 2023 he doesn't compare the England boots to Solovair directly. He says that on pure value the extra $90 over the Thailand-made pair is probably not worth it. Still, if you want something similar to how old Doc Martens were made, "you have to go made in England no question" [2]. He says right now "you have to be a mega fan to get them" [3].

**His earlier head-to-head (2022)**
- **Price:** he says Solovairs are actually cheaper than Made in England Docs [4].
- **Leather and midsoles:** he says the England boots' better leather should age fine and is probably on par with Solovair. He says the better midsoles are also probably on par [5].
- **Comfort and repair:** Solovairs have a shank, so they're a bit more comfortable over long periods. They're also Goodyear welted in a more regularly accepted way, so they're easier to resole [6].
- **Overall:** for pure value and a better-built boot, he says Solovair is the one to go for. The derby eight-eyed boot is essentially the same boot as the Dr. Martens one [7].
- **The one exception:** if the yellow stitching matters to you, you have to get the Made in England Docs [8].
- **Caveat:** his own Solovairs had a manufacturing defect after eight wears. A back tab ripped off and a lace snapped [9].

questions.question: Hi, I am going on a 4 day hike and I am wondering if I can use my blundstone for them, what do you think?

hybrid.answer:
He hasn't covered multi-day hiking in Blundstones in the videos available here. What he has said suggests they're fine for short outings but not ideal for serious hiking, so for four days he'd probably lean toward a proper hiking boot.

**What he says about hiking in them**
- In his one-year review he says they "are not good boots for mountaining apparently because they don't have uh good ankle support" [1]. He still took them up and down a few mountains in Maine, and they got a little scuffed but "held up well" [2].
- He calls them "decent for work boots but not anything incredible" [3]. His read is that Blundstones leaned into being a fashion boot rather than a more robust work or hiking boot.

**Comfort and break-in**
- He had no blisters walking around right after buying them [4]. But when he started running and walking the track in them, he got "big fat gross blisters like break-in blisters for boots" that stopped after two to three weeks [5]. If you go, make sure yours are properly broken in first.

**Water**
- They are water resistant, not waterproof. He says "blunt stones are not waterproof" [6], and that you can get them wet but shouldn't go swimming in them.
- In his pond test, his feet stayed dry apart from a little dampness at the elastic band. He says they're fine for crossing a brook or stream or standing in mud briefly, but he wouldn't stand in still water for long [7].
- As of 2023, his heavily worn pair remained "probably my most water resistant boots" [8]. In 2019 he said the water resistance depends on keeping the leather treated [9].

**Bottom line:** if your Blundstones are broken in and treated, they should cope with trails and some wet ground. He flags the lack of ankle support as the main drawback for mountain terrain.

questions.question: I'm 5'11-225 lbs with a dad bod. What's the most cost efficient and quality t shirt for me? Also, what size would u prefer?

hybrid.answer:
For your build, his pick is **Muji**, with **Uniqlo** as the cheaper alternative. He hasn't given a size recommendation for your height and weight, so I can only apply his stated rules.

**Cheapest good option: Uniqlo.** In his September 2025 roundup he says a $20 Uniqlo tee is probably the best t-shirt you can get for the price, bar none [1]. In mid-2025 he praised the bound neck collar and the price-to-quality ratio [2]. He calls it the "starter t-shirt" [3].

**For someone taller or wider: Muji.** He says to go Muji if you're taller or wider in any way. It costs about $4-5 more but is significantly longer and a good deal wider [3]. He says it's slightly tented out and that you'd probably like it if you're a little bigger [3]. In mid-2025 he also said the extra money feels justified, because the shirt feels better [4].

**Other value picks.**
- Front General Store is $40 and made in Japan. He is going with it on the day he filmed for the "best value" category [5].
- House of Blanks is $35 and made in Canada, with zero torque, which he calls an outstanding value [6].
- Kirkland is cheaper still, at about $4.20 a shirt. He calls it quite long and incredibly soft, but it shrank 4% in width and 2% in length [7].

**Size.** He gives no size for your build. Applying his rules, the Muji's extra length and width is his answer for bigger guys [3]. He also personally likes a lot of space across the shoulders in a tee [8]. He doesn't say whether to size up in Muji or Uniqlo.

questions.question: Am I the only one who loves these videos but in the end still has no idea which to buy? Please just tell me: buy this one, or these 3. I can't decide between 25 options. [t-shirts]

hybrid.answer:
He doesn't name one shirt to buy. His latest word (Sept 2025) is that nearly anyone can make a good tee now, so the best one is whichever matches your preferences [1]. He does give a short list of picks, though.

**If you want 3 to choose from, by what you want:**
- **Cheapest good one:** Uniqlo at $20, which he calls probably the best t-shirt you can get for the price [2]. If you're taller or wider, he says to get Muji instead [3].
- **Best value with more character:** Front General Store, a $40 shirt made in Japan [4]. He says that if you like character and feel, go with it, and that he's feeling it today [5].
- **Best value if you want perfectly smooth:** House of Blanks at $35, which showed zero torque in his test [6].

**His personal winner in each category (Sept 2025):**
- **All-arounders:** J. Press x American Trench, because he likes its rougher hand feel [7].
- **Japanese:** Wonder Looper, for its much better and more universal fit [8].
- **Heavyweight:** American Giant, which is lighter and fits more universally [8].
- **Minimalist/elevated:** Merz b. Schwanen 2M15, though Lady White could be his favorite and he says they're all great choices [9].

**Other notes:**
- In 2024 his overall winner was Asket [10]. In 2025 he says it's still very high up, but it didn't make the final list because that list was for shirts under $50 [11].
- He also says Bronson usually wins or comes close in other people's t-shirt comparisons [12].

If you want a single starting point from him, the value picks are the clearest answer: Uniqlo, Front General Store or House of Blanks.

questions.question: 1907 vs the 875's? What's the difference?

hybrid.answer:
**Short version:** The 1907 is the storm-welted version and the 875 is the Goodyear-welted one, with a few extras on the 1907 for about $10 more. In 2021 he called the 1907 the best Red Wing moc toe. By 2022–2023 he ranked neither above the other, and by then he preferred the 3335.

**Welt construction**
- **875:** It is Goodyear welted. He calls Goodyear welts "incredible", durable and fairly water resistant. The welt also leaves room for cork that molds to your foot [1][2].
- **1907:** It has a storm (Norwegian-like) welt, which he calls "invaluable" [3]. He says the popular view on Reddit is that Red Wing just stitches an extra leather strip onto the welt. He adds that he isn't quite sure and that a true Norwegian welt works differently [4].

**Price and extras**
- He says the 1907 costs about $10 more than the 875 [5].
- For that, he says you get Red Wing's removable leather footbed, which he says typically sells separately for $40. The footbed can be pulled out to help the boots dry [3].
- You also get leather laces, which he says are typically $15 [3].
- His conclusion is that the 1907 is the better deal [3].

**Soles**
- Both have crepe soles. He doesn't like them, and says a denser rubber sole won't break down as fast as crepe does [6][7].

**How his view changed**
- **2021:** He called the 1907 "red wings best heritage boots by far" and said to get it if you're looking at a Red Wing moc toe [8].
- **2022:** He said the 3335 beat both the 1907 and the 875 for him. He called the 1907 and 875 "more beefily constructed", so they are the ones to pick if you need a tough boot [9].
- **2023:** He said the 875, the 1907 and the Iron Rangers "all have their own characteristics that I really really like" [10]. He didn't rank them against each other.

He hasn't said which of the two he prefers after 2021.

questions.question: How does Uniqlo compare to The Front General Store,  Proclub, and Hanes? ie what is the best budget shirt?

hybrid.answer:
Uniqlo is the one he most often calls the best budget t-shirt. In September 2025 he said the $20 Uniqlo "is probably the best t-shirt that you can get bar none for the price" [1]. Front General Store is the step up he likes for feel and character. Hanes and Pro Club are older, more basic picks he reviewed in 2024.

**Uniqlo (newest view, 2025)**
- He calls it "your starter t-shirt". It's open-ended yarn and kind of rough [2].
- In June 2025 he said that at $15 it's very good, with a bound neck collar that doesn't wiggle. He added that the price-to-quality ratio is "insane" [5].
- In 2024 he gave it the best-value awards: the heavyweight crew for heavyweight or all-around, and the Supima tee for silky smooth [11].
- Its shrink test was about 2.3% in width and 2% in length [12].

**Front General Store**
- It's the shirt he picked for the most affordable category in his September 2025 roundup: "Today I'm feeling the Front General Store. Tomorrow I might be feeling House of Blanks." [3]
- He describes it as a $40, 100% made-in-Japan shirt with great proportions and great feel [4].
- In June 2025 he called it "still really good", at about $38 [6].
- In 2024 he said it was "one of the best shirts that you could possibly get" if you want a Japanese-made upgrade without spending over $40. He gave it 6/10 softness and noted it's pre-washed [10].
- So it costs about twice what Uniqlo does, and he picks it for character rather than price.

**Hanes**
- In 2024 he called it "your classic $10 great shirt". He gave it 7/10 softness and about 6.7% length shrink [8].
- In 2025 he said that, of five shirts he has from the very-low-price mass brands, he named "Hannes and Gild", and all five had a defect [7]. He didn't say which, if any, were Hanes.

**Pro Club**
- In 2024 he liked it, saying he likes everything about it. He called it the roughest shirt on that list [9].
- It had 4/10 softness and about 6.9% length shrink [9].
- He hasn't revisited it in the newer videos available here.

**Bottom line:** For pure value he leans Uniqlo. If you'd spend more for a Japanese-made shirt with more feel, he leans Front General Store. He also stresses that the "best" t-shirt depends on your preferences, since nearly everyone can make a good shirt now [13].

questions.question: Great video. But just curious, how can you say it's a con that the Huckberry jacket is unlined when they sell two different versions of lined waxed truckers: wool, and flannel?

hybrid.answer:
The unlined con comes from his 2023 video, and his newer 2025 video describes the Huckberry Flint and Tinder Waxed Trucker as lined. He has also since softened on unlined jackets in general. He hasn't said anything about a flannel-lined version.

**2025 (latest):** He calls the Flint and Tinder Waxed Trucker lined and says that's a plus: "It's lined, so that way it's comfortable. You don't get wax on your skin." [1] He also mentions a wool-lined version he hasn't gotten yet. [2] Those comments come in a Huckberry-sponsored segment, though he says he'd talked about this jacket many times before sponsorship. In the same video he says he usually wants a liner on wax jackets, but that "in my old age" he sees why you wouldn't line one. [3][4]

**2023:** He described the Huckberry jacket in that video as the "cheapest most simple unlined basic jacket" on his list. [5] The con was that Huckberry and Rogue Territory jackets "are not lined." He always likes a lining on wax jackets so the wax isn't touching your clothes or arms. [6] He still called the jacket fantastic overall.

**Not covered:** He hasn't discussed the flannel-lined version, and he hasn't explained how the unlined jacket in 2023 relates to the lined one in 2025.

questions.question: Do you know how these fit compared to the 875s? [Red Wing 3335s]

hybrid.answer:
He hasn't directly compared the fit of the 3335s to the 875s in the videos available here. He does describe how the 3335s fit, and what he says is mostly about the slim shape of the 3335.

**3335 fit:** He went true to size and says they fit fine [1]. He adds that the profile is very slim, because the outsole is very thin and the boots taper down [1]. With thin cotton socks in warm weather he had no tightness, but with wool socks his toes felt squished and he couldn't wiggle them much [1].

**How that relates to the 875:** The only contrast he draws is in build, not fit. He calls the 875s and 1907s "more beefily constructed" than the 3335s [2]. He doesn't say whether the 875 is roomier or tighter in the toes.

**Red Wing sizing in general:** In his 1907 review, he wore his usual size 8 in Red Wings and says they fit perfectly [3]. He suggests leather boots should fit snug but not squished [3]. That was about the 1907, not the 875 or the 3335.
